description: The plot illustrates the trade-off between perplexity and GPU memory usage as a function of the “Percent Sequence Ratio (%)” in the context of KV cache compression for LLM inference, as studied in the paper “PyramidInfer: Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM Inference.” The x-axis, labeled “Percent Sequence Ratio (%)”, spans from 0 to 100 in linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 20. The left y-axis, labeled “Perplexity”, ranges from 4.2 to 4.7 in linear scale with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, and the right y-axis, labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)”, spans from 0 to 100 in linear scale with tick marks at 10% intervals. Four curves are plotted: “Perplexity” (orange line with circle markers, solid) starts at ~4.6 at 0% and decreases to ~4.3 at 60%, then rises slightly to ~4.5 at 100%; “Full Cache PPL” (red dashed line) remains nearly flat around 4.4 across the entire range; “GPU Mem. Ratio” (blue line with circle markers, solid) increases steadily from ~40% at 0% to ~90% at 100%; and “Full Cache GPU Mem.” (blue dashed line) remains constant at ~90% across all sequence ratios. The plot visually demonstrates how reducing the sequence ratio (i.e., compressing the KV cache) lowers GPU memory usage while initially improving perplexity, before a slight degradation at higher compression levels.
